lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: relating domain to a quantitative context
lessonRef.title: Guided practice B: relating domain to a quantitative context

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read once, then cover the example and try the guided set from memory.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Does the set {(1, 4), (2, 4), (3, 4), (5, 4)} define y as a function of x? Justify the decision.
choices: Yes; repeated outputs are allowed, only repeated inputs with different outputs are not.
No; the input 4 gives both y = 2 and y = −2.
Yes; each input appears once, so each has exactly one output.
No; the input 1 is paired with both 3 and 8.

items.prompt: A machine starts with 115 components and consumes 5 per hour. It can run for at most 11 hours. What is the domain of C(h) = 115 − 5h in this context?
choices: all real numbers

items.prompt: A sequence is defined by a(1) = 9 and a(n) = a(n − 1) − 7 for n > 1. Find a(12).
In a modelling context, the graph of a cooling object’s temperature flattens out towards a horizontal line. Which feature is this, and what does it mean?
choices: an end behaviour approaching the surrounding temperature
an interval of increase
a zero, giving the time the object freezes
a maximum, giving the hottest temperature

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Does the set {(1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 7), (4, 9)} define y as a function of x? Justify the decision.
choices: Yes; repeated outputs are allowed, only repeated inputs with different outputs are not.
No; the input 1 is paired with both 3 and 8.
Yes; each input appears once, so each has exactly one output.
No; the input 4 gives both y = 2 and y = −2.

items.prompt: A machine starts with 35 components and consumes 4 per hour. It can run for at most 21 hours. What is the domain of C(h) = 35 − 4h in this context?
choices: all real numbers

items.prompt: A sequence is defined by a(1) = -5 and a(n) = a(n − 1) + 4 for n > 1. Find a(15).

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: In a modelling context, the graph of a projectile’s height against time crosses the horizontal axis. Which feature is this, and what does it mean?
choices: the y-intercept, giving the launch height
the average rate of change over the flight
a zero, giving the time the projectile returns to ground level
the maximum, giving the greatest height
